metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in New Philadelphia, OH | Tuscarawas County
metaDescription: New Philadelphia is the Tuscarawas County seat on the Utica flank. Learn how county-seat records and nearby activity shape a mineral rights sale.
heroLead: New Philadelphia is the Tuscarawas County seat, sitting on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, west of the thicker core in Carroll and Harrison counties, with the advantage of having the county's official land records right in town.
intro: Being the county seat means New Philadelphia is a practical starting point for anyone in Tuscarawas County trying to research mineral rights, whether the property in question is in town or out in the surrounding townships. The Tuscarawas County Recorder's office here holds the deed, lease, and severance records for the entire county.

sections.heading: Tuscarawas County's flank position and what it means
paragraphs: Tuscarawas sits west of Carroll and Harrison counties, generally in flank territory for the Utica/Point Pleasant play. That means activity here has been more selective, concentrated in specific townships rather than blanketing the whole county, so value on any given tract depends heavily on proximity to actual nearby units.

sections.heading: Coal history alongside oil and gas
paragraphs: Like much of this region, Tuscarawas County has a significant coal mining history in addition to oil and gas, and it's not unusual for coal rights and oil-and-gas rights to have been severed separately on the same tract. Confirming which specific rights you hold is a useful early step before any sale conversation.

sections.heading: Using the county seat location to your advantage
paragraphs: Since New Philadelphia is the county seat, in-person research at the recorder's office is straightforward for owners in the area. Pull your deed, check for any lease or severance filings, and confirm your exact ownership percentage before talking price with a buyer.

faqs.question: Is Tuscarawas County in the Utica core?
faqs.answer: Generally flank territory, west of the thicker core in Carroll and Harrison counties. Activity is more selective and concentrated in specific areas.

faqs.question: Where is the Tuscarawas County Recorder's office?
faqs.answer: It's located in New Philadelphia, the county seat, and holds deed, lease, and severance records for the entire county.

faqs.question: Could my coal rights and oil and gas rights be owned by different parties?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common in this region. Confirm which specific rights your family holds before assuming your mineral ownership is straightforward.

faqs.question: Can I research my mineral rights in person at the county seat?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since New Philadelphia is the Tuscarawas County seat, the recorder's office is local, which makes pulling deed, lease, and severance records more convenient than in counties where you'd need to travel.
